entries.claim: For two algebraic fractions with a common denominator, n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x), n2(x)=f3(x)/f2(x): the sum is (f1(x)+f3(x))/f2(x).
entries.quote: n1(x) = f1(x)/f2(x), n2(x) = f3(x)/f2(x) (two algebraic fractions having a common denominator)

entries.claim: With a common denominator, the difference is (f1(x) - f3(x))/f2(x), also written as f1(x)/f2(x) + (-f3(x))/f2(x).
For two algebraic fractions with different denominators, n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x), n2(x)=f3(x)/f4(x): the sum is (f1(x)×f4(x)+f3(x)×f2(x))/(f2(x)×f4(x)).
entries.quote: (two algebraica fractions having two different denominators)

entries.claim: With different denominators, the difference is (f1(x)×f4(x) - f3(x)×f2(x))/(f2(x)×f4(x)).

If n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x) and n2(x)=f3(x)/f4(x) are two algebraic fractions, then their product is the product of numerators over the product of denominators, where x is in the common domain of the two fractions, i.e. R − (Z(f2) ∪ Z(f4)).
entries.note: Both the rule (product of numerators over product of denominators) and the domain R − (Z(f2) ∪ Z(f4)) are explicitly stated in point ① of the yellow box.

entries.claim: Dividing two algebraic fractions means multiplying the first by the reciprocal of the second; the domain of n1 ÷ n2 is the common domain of n1, n2, n2^-1, i.e. R − (Z(f2) ∪ Z(f3) ∪ Z(f4)).
entries.note: Both the rule (division = multiplication by reciprocal) and the domain R − (Z(f2) ∪ Z(f3) ∪ Z(f4)) are explicitly stated in point ② of the yellow box.
